text:
**Short answer:** For most RVs, the **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** is the strongest all-around pick. If you mainly want to run a roof air conditioner on weekend trips, the **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** is simpler. On a tighter budget, the **BLUETTI AC200L** has a built-in 30A RV outlet. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

**Top options from the search results**

| Model | Capacity | Continuous / Surge | Best for | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 | 4,096 Wh (expandable past 12 kWh) | 4,000 W / 8,000 W | Full-time boondocking, roof AC plus home backup | [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) |
| Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro | 3,024 Wh | 3,000 W / 6,000 W | Running RV air conditioning | [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) |
| BLUETTI AC200L | 2,048 Wh | 2,400 W / 3,600 W | Budget pick with a 30A RV port | [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) |
| ALLPOWERS R4000 | 3,456 Wh | 3,600 W (120 V) / 6,000 W peak | Whole-RV backup, 2 kWh solar input | [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) |

A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500 W running and spikes past 3,000 W at startup, so look for a surge rating of roughly 3,000 W or more. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

**Choosing solar panels**

- **Match the station's solar input ceiling to your panels.** A rooftop array can be bottlenecked by a lower input limit. ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)) For example, the Bluetti AC200P tops out at 700 W, while the Jackery 2000 Plus accepts 1,400 W. ([Outdoor Power Stations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti))
- **The ALLPOWERS R4000 takes up to 2,000 W of solar** across three inputs, but only if you wire panels to all three. Each input maxes at 650 W. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh))
- **Portable panels work for smaller setups.** A 300–400 W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)) Renogy's 200 W foldable suitcase is one option mentioned. ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife))

**Things to check before buying**

- **Weight:** The R4000 weighs 45 kg and isn't meant to be carried by hand. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)) The DELTA Pro 3 is heavy enough that moving it is a two-person job. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- **Campground hookup:** Most campground pedestals are 30A. Confirm whether the unit has a 30A RV outlet or needs a TT-30 adapter.
- **Sources:** Several of these articles earn affiliate commissions. The Dealectric page also lists discount codes that the store may reject at checkout, so verify prices and codes on the manufacturer's site before buying.

I couldn't find verified direct retail links for the EcoFlow, Jackery, or BLUETTI models in these results, so check their official sites or a major retailer for current prices. The ALLPOWERS R4000 is the only unit with a direct store link here, and that page is affiliate-supported.
